summary: This section explains what happens after a company registers under this part of the Act. It treats existing laws and documents governing the company as its memorandum and articles. It also applies the rules of this Act to the company, its members, and creditors.
points: Existing laws and governing documents of the company act as if they are the registered memorandum and articles under this Act.
All provisions of this Act apply to the company, members, contributories, and creditors as if the company was formed under this Act.
Table F in Schedule I does not apply unless adopted by a special resolution.
Rules about numbering shares do not apply to a company whose shares are not numbered.
Specific rules apply to contributories and their legal representatives or assignees during a winding up.
The company cannot alter governing provisions that would have been required in the memorandum unless this Act allows it.
example: Asha Trading Private Limited decided to register under this Part of the Act. Previously, its internal rules were set out in a partnership deed. After registration, those rules are treated as if they were written into registered articles under the new Act. The general provisions of the Act now apply to Asha Trading Private Limited and its creditors. However, its unnumbered shares remain unnumbered because the specific rules about numbering shares do not apply to them. Later, when the company faced winding up, its members had to contribute towards debts contracted before registration just as the law required.

terms.meaning: The main document that sets out a company's constitution and basic conditions.
The document that contains the internal rules and regulations for managing a company.
A person liable to contribute to the assets of a company in the event of it being wound up.
The process of closing down a company and settling its affairs.

watch: Note that table F and share numbering rules have specific exceptions mentioned in the text.
